doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Sippie Wallace and Big Mama Thornton
title: Secret guest artists on albums
summary: The band never knew who the guest artist would be; Lockjaw arrived by surprise.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: And the guys never knew who our guest artist was going to be.
For any album we’ve ever done. They never know who the guest artists were.
Because oh they’d try to figure that out. They’d call and say well so-and-so, and who’s the guest artist? They’d try to get you to slip up.
But we wouldn’t tell them. When Lockjaw flew in from Las Vegas, and they were all, we were getting the stuff together in the studio and he came in. He said, “Gentlemen.” And they’re ahhhh.
That’s a great way to make people come to work too, man.
And they really played, because they wanted to impress him. They were so happy to see Jaw you know.
Oh it was a rush, you could feel it you know, a beautiful rush. Really wild.
I think you guys ought to write a book.
